A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a calixarene-based acylguanidinium catalyst with a suitable EM value can efficiently cleave phosphodiester bonds in RNA and DNA, and thus may find applications in the field of RNA and DNA sequencing and in the design of new RNA and DNA cleaving drugs.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a properly designed calixarene with acyguanidine units is a very effective catalyst for phosphodiaster bond cleavage, and it can be applied in the hydrolysis of RNA and DNA in a mild and efficient way.
